Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-ucs-uefi-sb-bypass-eb6xC5GW?vs_f=Cisco%20Security%20Advisory%26vs_cat=Security%20Intelligence%26vs_type=RSS%26vs_p=Cisco%20UCS%20and%20UCS-Based%20Appliances%20UEFI%20Shell%20Secure%20Boot%20Bypass%20Vulnerability%26vs_k=1

A vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances could allow an authenticated attacker with valid credentials for a user account with the role of user or admin or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access to an affected device to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks and execute unauthorized software.
This vulnerability is due to the availability of memory write commands in the UEFI Shell while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled on a device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by selecting the UEFI Shell boot option at boot time and using available shell commands to modify UEFI memory variables. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to manipulate the preboot environment, overwrite UEFI Secure Boot-related memory values, and execute unauthorized software on the affected device.

Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability.
This advisory is available at the following link:
https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-ucs-uefi-sb-bypass-eb6xC5GW

🌍 Iran, Belarus reaffirm commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation

📌 Moscow, IRNA — Iran’s newly appointed Ambassador to Belarus, Mohsen Omid-Zamani, has presented a copy of his credentials to Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov, reaffirming the two countries’ commitment to strengthening bilateral ties.

During the meeting in Minsk, the two sides discussed the latest developments and issues of mutual interest in political, economic, and trade relations, as well as cooperation within international and multilateral frameworks.
​
Omid-Zamanai and Ryzhenkov also emphasized their countries’ determination to maintain the positive and expanding trajectory of bilateral relations and highlighted the high level of mutual trust between Tehran and Minsk.
​
The officials stressed the importance of maintaining and strengthening political contacts and consultations at the highest levels to advance bilateral relations. They also called for regular dialogue aimed at deepening ties, expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation, and making greater use of existing capacities and opportunities.
​
Iran and Belarus have expanded cooperation across several sectors in recent years. On August 20, 2025, the two countries signed 12 cooperation documents in the presence of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and his Belarusian counterpart, Alexander Lukashenko.
​
The agreements covered political and legal affairs, tourism, culture, media, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, industry, environmental protection, free and special economic zones, investment, aviation, and education.
​
Other areas included medical sciences, forestry, veterinary health, standardization, metrology, accreditation, cinema, and cooperation between national news agencies and broadcasters, reflecting the broadening scope of Tehran–Minsk relations.
